easy.def: A tool that tells how heavy something is.
examples: I stand on the scale.
The scale shows my weight.
The scale says five pounds.

more.def: A tool for measuring how heavy something is.
examples: I stood on the scale at the doctor.
The scale showed that the melon weighed five pounds.
She put the fruit on the scale.

easy.def: A thin, hard plate on a fish or snake.
examples: The fish has scales.
A snake has scales.
The scale is shiny.

more.def: One of the small, hard, flat plates that cover the skin of a fish, snake or lizard.
examples: The fish's scales shone in the sun.
A snake is covered in dry scales.
The dragon in the story had green scales.

easy.def: A set of musical notes that go up or down.
examples: I practice the scale.
The piano scale is hard.
She sang a scale.

more.def: A series of musical notes that go up or down in order.
examples: I practiced the C scale on the piano.
She sang a scale from low to high.
The teacher had us play a scale.

easy.def: The skin on your head under your hair.
examples: My scalp is itchy.
She washed her scalp.
A sore scalp.

more.def: The skin on the top of your head that is covered by hair.
examples: My scalp itched from the sun.
She rubbed shampoo into her scalp.
The barber checked his scalp.

easy.def: A very small, sharp knife that doctors use.
examples: The doctor used a scalpel.
A scalpel is sharp.
The scalpel is small.

more.def: A small, very sharp knife used by surgeons in operations.
examples: The surgeon held a scalpel.
A scalpel is very sharp and used with great care.
The scalpel cut cleanly through the skin.

easy.def: A trick to steal money.
examples: The scam fooled people.
It was a scam.
Do not fall for the scam.

more.def: A dishonest plan to trick people and take their money.
examples: The email was a scam to steal money.
Do not fall for a scam.
Police warned people about the scam.

easy.def: To look quickly over something.
examples: I scan the page.
She scanned the room for her friend.
He scanned the list.

more.def: To look quickly over something to find a certain thing, or to copy it with a machine.
examples: He scanned the menu for something he liked.
He scanned the page for his name.
The clerk scanned the bar code at the store.

easy.def: A shocking event that makes people angry.
examples: The scandal was in the news.
The scandal upset the town.
The scandal ended his job.

more.def: An event in which someone does something wrong that shocks the public.
examples: The scandal was in the news for weeks.
A scandal at the bank upset the town.
The mayor left her job after the scandal.

easy.def: A mark left on skin after a cut heals.
examples: I have a scar on my knee.
The scar is small.
He got a scar from falling.

more.def: A mark that stays on the skin after an injury has healed.
examples: I have a scar on my knee from falling off my bike.
The old scar looked like a thin line.
The tree had a scar where a branch broke off.

easy.def: To make someone afraid.
examples: The loud noise scared me.
Do not scare the cat.
The ghost story scares him.

more.def: To make a person or animal feel afraid.
examples: The thunder scared the puppy.
Don't scare the birds away.
The movie scared the little kids.

easy.def: Afraid.
examples: The puppy is scared of thunder.
I felt scared in the dark.
She was scared of the big dog.

more.def: Feeling fear because you think something bad may happen.
examples: He felt scared when the lights went out.
The kitten was scared by the loud noise.
She was scared to jump into the deep end.

easy.def: A long cloth worn around your neck.
examples: I wear a scarf in winter.
The scarf is warm.
She knitted a scarf.

more.def: A long piece of cloth that you wear around your neck to keep warm.
examples: I wore a wool scarf to keep warm.
Grandma knitted me a red scarf.
The wind blew her scarf away.

easy.def: A bright red color.
examples: She wore a scarlet hat.
The fire truck is scarlet.
I found a scarlet leaf.

more.def: Bright red with a little orange in it, like a ripe tomato or a cardinal's feathers.
examples: The cardinal's scarlet feathers stood out against the white snow.
Her cheeks turned scarlet when she forgot her lines in the play.
The maple leaves turned scarlet and gold in October.

easy.def: A bright red color.
examples: I painted the door scarlet.
Scarlet is my favorite color.
The curtains were a deep scarlet.

more.def: A very bright red color that looks a little orange, like a ripe tomato.
examples: The sunset glowed in shades of scarlet and orange over the lake.
The knights carried banners of scarlet and gold into the castle.
She mixed red and yellow paint to make a rich scarlet.

easy.def: Making you feel afraid.
examples: The dark cave was scary.
I told a scary story.
The thunder is scary.

more.def: Causing fear, so that you feel nervous or frightened.
examples: The old haunted house looked scary at night.
The roller coaster was scary but fun.
Some kids find big dogs scary until they get to know them.

easy.def: To throw or move things all over.
examples: We scatter seeds for the birds.
The wind scatters the leaves.
The birds scattered when the cat came.

more.def: To throw or spread things over a wide area, or to move apart quickly.
examples: The marbles scattered across the floor when the bag broke.
The crowd scattered when the rain began.
He scattered salt on the icy steps.

easy.def: An imagined set of events.
examples: We acted out a scenario.
The scenario is pretend.
Think of a scenario.

more.def: A description of events that might happen.
examples: We acted out a scenario where we got lost.
In the best scenario, it will not rain.
The teacher gave us a scenario to solve.

easy.def: A view of a place.
examples: The beach was a nice scene.
It was a pretty winter scene.
The painting shows a farm scene.

more.def: A view of a place and the things in it, as in a picture.
examples: The painting shows a quiet farm scene.
We looked at the snowy winter scene from the window.
A pretty scene of mountains and a lake hung on the wall.

easy.def: A part of a play or movie.
examples: The first scene was funny.
My scene is next.
She forgot her lines in the scene.

more.def: One part of a play, movie or book that happens in one place or time.
examples: In the first scene, the curtain rose on a forest.
The funniest scene in the movie was the food fight.
We rehearsed the last scene again.

easy.def: The natural things you see in a place, such as hills and trees.
examples: The scenery is lovely.
We admired the scenery.
I like the scenery here.

more.def: The natural view of a place, such as mountains, trees and rivers; or the painted scenes on a stage.
examples: We enjoyed the beautiful scenery on our drive.
The scenery of the mountains took our breath away.
The stage crew painted the scenery for the school play.

easy.def: A smell.
examples: I like the scent of roses.
The dog follows a scent.
The scent of pine.

more.def: A smell, especially a pleasant one.
examples: I love the scent of fresh bread.
The dog followed the scent of a rabbit.
The scent of pine filled the cabin.

easy.def: A list of times for things.
examples: The bus schedule is here.
Check the schedule.
Our schedule is busy.

more.def: A list that shows when things will happen.
examples: The bus schedule shows when the next bus comes.
Check the schedule to see when the game starts.
Our class has a busy schedule on Fridays.

easy.def: A plan, often a clever or secret one.
examples: The villain had a scheme.
They made a scheme.
The scheme worked.

more.def: A plan for doing something, especially one that is clever or secret.
examples: The villain in the story had a sneaky scheme.
The friends made a scheme to surprise their teacher.
The color scheme of the room is blue and white.

easy.def: A person who studies a lot.
examples: The scholar read many books.
A scholar studied the old map.
She wants to be a scholar.

more.def: A person who studies a subject very deeply and knows a great deal about it.
examples: The scholar spent years studying ancient languages.
A famous scholar gave a talk about the history of the town.
The library was full of scholars reading old books.

easy.def: Money that helps pay for school.
examples: She won a scholarship.
The scholarship pays for college.
He got a scholarship.

more.def: Money given to a student to help pay for school because they did well or need help.
examples: She won a scholarship to go to college.
The scholarship pays for his books and classes.
A music scholarship helped her learn the violin.

easy.def: A place where children go to learn.
examples: I walk to school.
School starts at eight.
Our school is big.

more.def: A place where students go to learn from teachers.
examples: Our school has a library, a gym, and a garden.
The school bus picks us up at the corner.
She goes to school five days a week.

easy.def: A person who teaches at a school.
examples: My aunt is a schoolteacher.
The schoolteacher gave homework.
He wants to be a schoolteacher.

more.def: A person whose job is to teach children at a school.
examples: My aunt is a schoolteacher who teaches third grade.
The schoolteacher handed out the math tests.
He wants to be a schoolteacher when he grows up.

easy.def: Learning about the world by testing ideas.
examples: I like science class.
Science is fun.
We do science tests.

more.def: The study of how the world works, using careful tests and observation.
examples: We learned about volcanoes in science class.
Science helps us understand weather.
She wants to study science when she grows up.

easy.def: Having to do with science.
examples: We did a scientific test.
The scientific book is long.
The scientific name is long.

more.def: Having to do with science, or using careful tests and facts.
examples: The class did a scientific experiment with plants.
The scientific name for a dog is Canis lupus familiaris.
A scientific test needs careful notes.

easy.def: A person who studies how the world works.
examples: The scientist looked in a microscope.
Scientists study space.
I want to be a scientist.

more.def: A person who studies nature and the world through careful tests and observations.
examples: The scientist put the water under the microscope.
Scientists study volcanoes to learn how they work.
She became a scientist who studies whales.

easy.def: A tool with two blades for cutting paper.
examples: I cut with scissors.
The scissors are sharp.
Hand me the scissors.

more.def: A tool with two sharp blades joined in the middle that you use to cut paper or cloth.
examples: I cut the paper with scissors.
The scissors are sharp, so be careful.
She trimmed the thread with the scissors.

easy.def: To tell someone off for doing something wrong.
examples: Mom scolded the dog.
The teacher scolded us.
She scolded him for being late.

more.def: To tell someone in an angry voice that they have done something wrong.
examples: Mom scolded me for leaving my muddy boots on the carpet.
The teacher scolded the class for talking during the test.
Dad scolded the puppy for chewing his shoe.

easy.def: A tool or amount that you lift up.
examples: I want a scoop of ice cream.
The scoop is big.
I used a scoop.

more.def: A tool like a deep spoon for lifting things, or the amount it holds.
examples: I ordered two scoops of ice cream.
She used a scoop to measure the flour.
He filled the bucket with a scoop of sand.

easy.def: To lift something up with a tool or your hand.
examples: I scoop the ice cream.
She scooped up the sand.
He scooped the water.

more.def: To pick up or dig out something using a curved tool or your hand.
examples: I scooped the ice cream into a bowl.
She scooped up the sand with her hands.
He scooped the soup into bowls.

easy.def: To move quickly along.
examples: Scoot over and make room.
The mouse scooted away.
I scooted across the floor.

more.def: To move quickly or to slide a short way, often a little at a time.
examples: Scoot over so your friend can sit next to you on the bench.
The squirrel scooted up the tree when it heard a noise.
The baby scooted across the floor on her bottom.

easy.def: A toy you stand on and push with one foot.
examples: I ride my scooter to the park.
The scooter has two wheels.
She pushed her scooter up the hill.

more.def: A toy with two small wheels and a handle that you stand on and push along with one foot, or a small motorized vehicle like it.
examples: I glided down the sidewalk on my scooter.
He wore a helmet and knee pads when he rode his scooter.
The man rode a small motor scooter through the narrow village street.

easy.def: How far something reaches.
examples: The scope of the project is large.
That is beyond my scope.
The scope of the job is small.

more.def: The size or range of something that is covered.
examples: The scope of the project is very large.
That job is outside the scope of my work.
The scope of the test includes all of chapter one.

easy.def: The number of points in a game.
examples: The score is two to one.
What is the score?
Our team has a high score.

more.def: The number of points a person or team has in a game.
examples: The score was tied at three.
What was the score of the game?
She got a perfect score on the test.

easy.def: To get a point.
examples: I scored a goal.
She scores in every game.
He scored a run.

more.def: To get a point or points in a game.
examples: She scored two goals in the soccer game.
He scored the winning run.
Our team scored in the last minute.

easy.def: A small desert animal with eight legs and a tail that can sting.
examples: A scorpion hid under the rock.
The scorpion has a tail.
I saw a scorpion at the museum.

more.def: A small animal related to spiders, with claws like a crab and a tail that can sting, found in warm dry places.
examples: A scorpion hid under a rock to escape the hot sun.
The scorpion raised its tail as the beetle came near.
We saw a glowing scorpion under a special light at the museum.

easy.def: A person sent ahead to find things out.
examples: The scout looked for a path.
The scout rode ahead.
A scout watched for danger.

more.def: A person who goes ahead of a group to find out what is there.
examples: The scout rode ahead to find a safe path.
A scout climbed the hill to look around.
The explorers sent a scout to find water.

easy.def: A member of a youth group that learns outdoor skills.
examples: I am in the scouts.
The scouts went camping.
She is a scout.

more.def: A young person in a group that teaches outdoor skills and helping others.
examples: The scouts went camping by the lake.
My brother is a scout and earned a badge.
The scouts picked up trash in the park.

easy.def: To go away fast.
examples: The cat scrammed.
We scram when it rains.
The kids scrammed.

more.def: To leave quickly, often when told to.
examples: The cat scrammed when the dog barked.
We scrammed when it started to rain.
The kids scrammed when they saw the teacher coming.

easy.def: To climb or move quickly using your hands and feet.
examples: We scramble over the rocks.
The kids scrambled up the hill.
She scrambled out of bed.

more.def: To move or climb quickly and awkwardly, often using your hands as well.
examples: We scrambled over the rocks to the top.
The kids scrambled up the steep hill.
She scrambled out of bed when the alarm rang.

easy.def: To mix up, as eggs.
examples: Dad scrambles eggs.
I scrambled the eggs.
We ate scrambled eggs.

more.def: To cook eggs by stirring them in a pan, or to mix things up.
examples: Dad scrambles eggs for breakfast.
I scrambled two eggs in the pan.
The letters were scrambled, so we had to put them in order.

related.def: To put back in the right order.

easy.def: Mixed up.
examples: I like scrambled eggs.
The letters are scrambled.
The scrambled eggs are hot.

more.def: Mixed together, as eggs that are stirred while they cook.
examples: I like scrambled eggs for breakfast.
The letters on the board were scrambled.
Mom served scrambled eggs and toast.

easy.def: A small piece.
examples: I found a scrap of paper.
The dog got scraps.
The scrap of cloth is red.

more.def: A small piece or bit that is left over.
examples: I wrote the number on a scrap of paper.
The dog ate the scraps from dinner.
She sewed a quilt from scraps of cloth.

easy.def: To rub against something rough.
examples: I scraped my knee.
She scraped the paint.
He scraped the mud off his shoes.

more.def: To rub something along a rough surface, or to remove something by rubbing.
examples: I scraped my knee on the sidewalk.
She scraped the old paint off the wall.
He scraped the mud off his boots.

easy.def: A small hurt where skin was rubbed.
examples: I have a scrape on my knee.
The scrape is small.
A scrape stung.

more.def: A small injury on the skin from rubbing against something rough.
examples: I have a scrape on my knee from falling.
The scrape healed in a few days.
Mom put a bandage on my scrape.

easy.def: To rub with your nails.
examples: I scratch my arm.
The cat scratched the chair.
The dog scratches its ear.

more.def: To rub or scrape something with fingernails or claws.
examples: The cat scratched the couch.
The dog scratched its ear.
I scratched the itchy bite.

easy.def: A thin mark or small cut.
examples: There is a scratch on the car.
I have a scratch on my arm.
The cat left a scratch.

more.def: A thin mark or shallow cut made by something sharp.
examples: There is a scratch on the car door.
The thorn left a scratch on my arm.
The cat left a scratch on the table.

easy.def: To yell in a loud, high voice.
examples: She screamed when she saw the spider.
The kids scream on the ride.
We screamed with joy.

more.def: To make a loud, high cry because you are scared, excited or hurt.
examples: The riders screamed with excitement on the roller coaster.
She screamed when a mouse ran by.
The baby screamed for a bottle.

easy.def: A loud, high cry.
examples: I heard a scream.
A scream came from the ride.
His scream was loud.

more.def: A loud, high cry of fear, pain or excitement.
examples: A scream came from the roller coaster.
We heard a scream from the haunted house.
She let out a scream of joy.

easy.def: To make a high, harsh sound.
examples: The tires screeched.
The owl screeched.
The brakes screech.

more.def: To make a loud, high, harsh noise.
examples: The tires screeched as the car stopped.
An owl screeched in the night.
The chalk screeched on the board.

easy.def: The flat part of a TV or computer that shows pictures.
examples: I looked at the screen.
The TV screen is big.
The screen is bright.

more.def: The flat part of a television, phone or computer that shows pictures and words.
examples: The movie played on a huge screen.
Too much time in front of a screen can make your eyes tired.
The screen showed a picture of the moon.

easy.def: A net on a window that keeps bugs out.
examples: Close the screen door.
A bug is on the screen.
The screen has a hole.

more.def: A frame with a fine net in it that covers a window or door to keep out insects.
examples: The screen on the window kept the mosquitoes out.
Dad patched a hole in the porch screen.
A moth rested on the screen door.

easy.def: A showing of a film for an audience.
examples: We went to a screening.
The screening is at seven.
The school had a movie screening.

more.def: A showing of a movie or film for an audience.
examples: We went to a screening of the new cartoon.
The school held a screening of a movie on Friday night.
The screening starts at seven in the evening.

easy.def: A check to see if people are healthy or safe.
examples: The nurse did a hearing screening.
A vision screening is quick.
We had a screening at school.

more.def: A check done on many people to find any health problem early.
examples: The nurse did a hearing screening at school.
A vision screening takes only a few minutes.
Every student had a health screening in the fall.

easy.def: A thin metal pin with a twisty edge.
examples: Dad used a screw to hang the shelf.
The screw is loose.
I found a screw on the floor.

more.def: A small metal pin with a spiral edge that is twisted into wood or metal to hold things together.
examples: Dad drove a screw into the wall to hang the picture.
A loose screw made the chair wobble.
A box of screws sat on the workbench.

easy.def: To twist something on tight.
examples: Screw the lid on.
Dad screwed the shelf to the wall.
Screw in the light bulb.

more.def: To fasten something by twisting it, or by using a metal pin with a spiral edge.
examples: Screw the lid on tightly so the jam does not spill.
Dad screwed the hook into the beam.
She screwed the bulb into the lamp.

easy.def: The words that actors say in a play or movie.
examples: The actors read the script.
I forgot my lines in the script.
The script has the words.

more.def: The written words of a play, movie or show, telling the actors what to say and do.
examples: The actors learned their lines from the script.
She wrote a script for a puppet show.
The director gave everyone a copy of the script.

easy.def: A long paper rolled up.
examples: The scroll was very old.
He unrolled the scroll.
A scroll hung on the wall.

more.def: A long roll of paper or parchment with writing on it.
examples: The museum had an ancient scroll in a glass case.
He unrolled the scroll and read the message aloud.
People once wrote books on long scrolls instead of pages.

easy.def: To move text on a screen up or down.
examples: I scroll down the page.
Scroll to the top.
She scrolled through the pictures.

more.def: To move what is on a computer or phone screen up or down to see more.
examples: I scrolled down the page to find the answer.
He scrolled through the photos on the tablet.
Scroll to the top of the page to start again.

easy.def: To rub hard to clean.
examples: I scrub the pot.
She scrubbed the floor.
Scrub your hands.

more.def: To rub something hard with a brush to get it clean.
examples: I scrubbed the muddy boots.
She scrubbed the pot until it shone.
Scrub your hands with soap before dinner.

related.def: A brush or pad for scrubbing.

easy.def: To crush or squeeze up.
examples: I scrunch my nose.
She scrunched the paper.
He scrunched up his face.

more.def: To squeeze or crumple something into a tight shape.
examples: I scrunched my nose at the smell.
She scrunched the paper into a ball.
He scrunched up his face at the sour taste.

easy.def: A piece of art that is carved or made into a shape.
examples: The sculpture was made of clay.
We saw a sculpture.
The sculpture is tall.

more.def: A piece of art made by carving, shaping or joining things such as stone, clay or metal.
examples: The sculpture was carved from a block of stone.
We saw a giant metal sculpture in the park.
She made a clay sculpture of her cat.
